original_source_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-compute-cohomology-on-sheaf-sets}
Let $(\mathcal{C}, \mathcal{O})$ be a ringed site.
Let $K$ be a presheaf of sets on $\mathcal{C}$.
Let $\mathcal{F}$ be an $\mathcal{O}$-module and denote
$\mathcal{F}_{ab}$ the underlying sheaf of abelian groups.
Then $H^p(K, \mathcal{F}) = H^p(K, \mathcal{F}_{ab})$.

final_content.statement:
For a presheaf of sets $K$ on a site $\mathcal C$ and an $\mathcal O$-module $\mathcal F$, define $\mathcal F(K)=\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathrm{PSh}(\mathcal C)}(K,\mathcal F)$ and $H^p(K,\mathcal F)=R^p(\mathcal F\mapsto\mathcal F(K))$ in $\mathrm{Mod}(\mathcal O)$. For the underlying abelian sheaf $\mathcal F_{ab}$ use the analogous derived functor in $\mathrm{Ab}(\mathcal C)$.

Let $(\mathcal{C}, \mathcal{O})$ be a ringed site.
Let $K$ be a presheaf of sets on $\mathcal{C}$.
Let $\mathcal{F}$ be an $\mathcal{O}$-module and denote
$\mathcal{F}_{ab}$ the underlying sheaf of abelian groups.
Then $H^p(K, \mathcal{F}) = H^p(K, \mathcal{F}_{ab})$.
hypotheses: $(\mathcal C,\mathcal O)$ is a ringed site.
$K$ is a presheaf of sets on $\mathcal C$.
$\mathcal F$ is an $\mathcal O$-module; $\mathcal F_{ab}$ is its underlying abelian sheaf.
conclusions: For all $p\ge0$, $H^p_{\mathrm{Mod}(\mathcal O)}(K,\mathcal F)\cong H^p_{\mathrm{Ab}(\mathcal C)}(K,\mathcal F_{ab})$.

semantic_review_note: For a ringed site, presheaf K and O-module F, cohomology derived from K-sections agrees as abelian groups with that of the underlying abelian sheaf. The candidate accurately defines the K-section right-derived functors in each category and retains every degree p≥0.

original_source_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-cech-to-cohomology-sheaf-sets}
Let $\mathcal{C}$ be a site. Let $K' \to K$ be a map of presheaves
of sets on $\mathcal{C}$ whose sheafification is surjective. Set
$K'_p = K' \times_K \ldots \times_K K'$ ($p + 1$-factors).
For every abelian sheaf $\mathcal{F}$ there is a spectral sequence
with $E_1^{p, q} = H^q(K'_p, \mathcal{F})$ converging to
$H^{p + q}(K, \mathcal{F})$.

final_content.statement:
For a presheaf of sets $K$ on a site, cohomology $H^q(K,\mathcal F)$ means the right derived functor of $\mathcal F\mapsto\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathrm{PSh}(\mathcal C)}(K,\mathcal F)$ in the abelian-sheaf category. Given $K'\to K$, set $K'_p=(K')^{\times_K(p+1)}$ in presheaves. Surjectivity of the **sheafification** $(K')^\#\to K^\#$ is assumed; the original presheaf map need not be pointwise surjective.

Let $\mathcal{C}$ be a site. Let $K' \to K$ be a map of presheaves
of sets on $\mathcal{C}$ whose sheafification is surjective. Set
$K'_p = K' \times_K \ldots \times_K K'$ ($p + 1$-factors).
For every abelian sheaf $\mathcal{F}$ there is a spectral sequence
with $E_1^{p, q} = H^q(K'_p, \mathcal{F})$ converging to
$H^{p + q}(K, \mathcal{F})$.
hypotheses: $K'\to K$ is a map of presheaves of sets for which $(K')^\#\to K^\#$ is an epimorphism of sheaves.
$\mathcal F$ is an abelian sheaf on $\mathcal C$.
conclusions: There is a spectral sequence $E_1^{p,q}=H^q(K'_p,\mathcal F)$, with $K'_p=(K')^{\times_K(p+1)}$, converging to $H^{p+q}(K,\mathcal F)$.

semantic_review_note: For a presheaf map K'→K with surjective SHEAFIFICATION, its fiber-product Cech nerve K'_p gives a spectral sequence E1^{p,q}=H^q(K'_p,F) converging to H^{p+q}(K,F). The candidate explicitly distinguishes sheafification surjectivity from pointwise surjectivity.

original_source_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-cohomology-on-sheaf-sets}
Let $\mathcal{C}$ be a site. Let $K$ be a sheaf of sets on $\mathcal{C}$.
Consider the morphism of topoi
$j : \Sh(\mathcal{C}/K) \to \Sh(\mathcal{C})$, see
Sites, Lemma \ref{sites-lemma-localize-topos-site}.
Then $j^{-1}$ preserves injectives and
$H^p(K, \mathcal{F}) = H^p(\mathcal{C}/K, j^{-1}\mathcal{F})$
for any abelian sheaf $\mathcal{F}$ on $\mathcal{C}$.
